easy.def: To walk around with no place to go.
examples: We wander in the park.
The cows wander in the field.
Do not wander away from me.

more.def: To move around slowly without a clear direction or purpose.
examples: The lost puppy wandered through the streets.
We wandered around the market looking at the stalls.
His mind wandered during the long speech.
The sign warns us that the floor is wet.
Mom warned me the pan was hot.
The bell warns us of a fire.

more.def: To tell someone about a possible danger or problem before it happens.
examples: The lifeguard warned the swimmers about the strong waves.
Dark clouds warned us that a storm was coming.
The sign warns drivers of a sharp turn ahead.
The wealthy queen had lots of gold.
The wealthy man had a big house.
She is wealthy but lives simply.

more.def: Having a lot of money or valuable things; rich.
examples: A wealthy family gave money to build the new library.
The wealthy merchant owned ten ships.
It is one of the wealthiest cities in the world.
The weary boy fell asleep.
The weary dog lay down.
I am weary after the long day.

more.def: Very tired, especially after working hard or for a long time.
examples: The weary travelers were glad to finally reach the inn.
The weary nurse had worked all night.
She gave a weary sigh and sat down.

easy.def: What it is like outside, like sunny or rainy.
examples: The weather is sunny today.
We play inside in bad weather.
I like snowy weather.

more.def: What the air outside is like at a certain time, such as hot, cold, rainy, or windy.
examples: We checked the weather before planning our picnic.
The game was called off because of bad weather.
The weather in the mountains can change quickly.

easy.def: To talk in a very soft voice.
examples: Whisper so you do not wake the baby.
She whispered in my ear.
We whisper in the library.

more.def: To speak very softly, using your breath instead of your full voice.
examples: He whispered the secret into his sister's ear.
The children whispered so they would not wake the baby.
The wind whispered through the tall grass.

easy.def: Living in nature, not with people.
examples: A wolf is a wild animal.
Wild birds sing in the trees.
A wild horse ran free.

more.def: Living or growing in nature without being cared for by people.
examples: We picked wild berries along the trail.
Wild horses still live on the island.
The garden grew wild after no one looked after it.

easy.def: Knowing what is good and right to do.
examples: Grandma has a lot of wisdom.
The old owl in the story has wisdom.
There is wisdom in that old saying.

more.def: Good sense and judgment that comes from knowledge and experience.
examples: The old story is full of wisdom about being kind.
People came from far away to hear the teacher's wisdom.
With age comes wisdom, my grandmother says.

easy.def: Knowing a lot and making good choices.
examples: My grandpa is wise.
The wise old owl gave good advice.
It is wise to wear a coat in the cold.

more.def: Having good judgment and knowing what is right, often from experience.
examples: It was wise to bring a raincoat on such a cloudy day.
The wise queen listened before she decided.
He made a wise choice to save his money.

easy.def: To think about something and want to know more.
examples: I wonder why the sky is blue.
I wonder what is for lunch.
She wonders where birds sleep.

more.def: To think about something with curiosity, wanting to know the answer.
examples: She wondered how deep the ocean really was.
He wondered if he had locked the door.
I wonder what the world will be like in fifty years.

easy.def: Thinking that something bad might happen.
examples: I am worried about my sick cat.
Mom was worried when I was late.
The worried dog waited by the door.

more.def: Feeling uneasy because you think something bad might happen.
examples: He was worried that he would miss the bus.
The farmer is worried about the lack of rain.
She gave me a worried look.

easy.def: A small line or fold in skin or cloth.
examples: My shirt has a wrinkle.
Grandpa has wrinkles by his eyes.
I smooth the wrinkle in the paper.

more.def: A small line or fold in skin, cloth, or paper.
examples: She ironed the shirt to take out the wrinkles.
The map had deep wrinkles from being folded.
Laughing makes little wrinkles appear around her eyes.
